To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fast ignition driven by quasi monoenergetic ion beams can achieve ignition of compressed Deuterum-Tritium with energies that scale as Z2, and that a combination of 5.5GeV vanadium ion beam and a new irradiation geometry can reduce the required number of ions by 3 orders of magnitude.

fast ignition of inertial confinement fusion driven by quasi-monomergetic ion beams requires ion energies scaling with Z2, and that the ignition energies can be reduced by three orders of magnitude using a combination of intermediate ions and a new irradiation strategy.

(1) The ignition energy is almost independent on the atomic number of the ions; (2) the ignition energy increases as Z2, with the ion atomic number Z, when the ion energy is kept fixed; (3) the optimal ion energy scales as Z2; and (4) the ignition energy is reduced by three orders of magnitude by combining an ion beam array with intermediate Z ions and by increasing the ion energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the optimal ion type and the reduction of the required number of ions to ignite an ideal configuration of a compressed Deuterium-Tririum target by using an ion beam array.
the development of a fast ignition scheme for inertial confinement fusion, driven by quasi-monomergetic heavy ion beams.
the optimization of ion beam driven fast ignition of inertial confinement fusion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of a 10?m spot size, the optimal ion type is the one with Z2 = 10 GeV.
the optimal ion type is the one that minimizes the ignition energy per particle and that, for the present configuration, it corresponds to intermediate Z ions, like vanadium.
the fast ignition scheme driven by quasi-monomergetic ion beams, with an ion energy of 5.5GeV and a spot size of 10?m, is the most promising one for the realization of inertial fusion energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fast ignition driven by quasi-monoegetic ion beams is a promising scheme for inertial fusion energy.
the fast ignition scheme with quasi-monoenergetics ions is a promising alternative to the proton scheme, especially for the use of intermediate Z ions and the new irradiated scheme.

, in the case of fast ignition driven by quasi-monochromatic ion beams, the minimum ignition energies can be reduced by increasing the ion energy and/or by increasing the atomic number of the ion species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal ion atomic number for fast ignition driven by quasi monoenergetic beams is not necessarily the highest possible.
, in principle, fast ignition driven by quasi- monoenergetic ion beams could be an alternative to proton fast ignition.
the ignition energies can be reduced by orders of magnitude if the ions are focused into spots of the order of 10?m.
